time_convention: t = frame / 24; frame = round(t*24); frame 0 is t=0
units: pixels and seconds; no metric scale guessed

camera.evidence: phase correlation of the raccoon-free top strip (rows 0-600) against frame 0: |shift| < 0.25 px for every frame tested (0,10,...,70,71)

background.description: seamless grey studio cyclorama (dark vignetted wall, lighter floor), no markings, no other objects
background.ground_contact_line_note: top of the raccoon's dark contact shadow when feet are down; the ground line where its feet touch. Horizontal, constant over the clip -> motion is in a plane facing the camera, no visible perspective change of the raccoon (bbox width stays 316-333 px).

objects.name: raccoon
objects.description: single grey raccoon with ringed (banded) tail and pale face/snout, running in profile left->right (facing +x / right)
objects.reference_point: cx_mask, cy_mask = centroid of the segmented silhouette (stand-in for the rig origin; the true rig root is not visible, see notes). Horizontal motion is identical for any body-fixed point up to gait wobble.

body_length_without_tail_approx.reliability: rough, +-25 px (tail-base split by column thickness, hind legs confuse it)

motion_summary_px.direction: +x (rightwards), essentially horizontal; centroid y bobs between ~781 and ~795 with the gait
motion_summary_px.note: pace is close to uniform (quadratic fit of cx_mask vs frame gives a2 = 0.0014 px/frame^2, i.e. negligible acceleration); per-frame centroid steps fluctuate +-2.5 px with the gait

events.event: frames 0 and 1 are identical (raccoon has not moved yet); motion starts between frame 1 and frame 2
steady gallop/run left->right through the end of the clip; no stop, bounce, turn or contact with other objects
gait cycle: bbox height peaks (tail raised, back arched) at frames 0-1, 16-17, 32, 47, 62-63 -> stride period ~15.3 frames (~0.64 s)
raccoon exits nothing / enters nothing: fully in frame the whole clip (x from 534 to 2429)

files.scripts/: bg.py (median background), track.py (segmentation + CSV + overlays), summary.py, static_and_plot.py, probe.py
